title: Psychosocial needs and supportive care needs after subarachnoid hemorrhage: Detection and evaluation
summary: Project Objectives: The primary objective of the PERSUADE project is to conduct an exploratory assessment of the gaps in care related to psychological, cognitive, and social stress following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhages (aSAB). Using a mixed-methods design (qualitative interviews, focus groups, and quantitative questionnaires), these burdens and support needs will be evaluated from the perspectives of patients, family members, and healthcare providers. These findings will pave the way for follow-up projects aimed at developing and validating targeted interventions for the psychological, cognitive, and social consequences of aSAB.

interventions.name:
Guided, qualitative interviews with patients following an aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
Standardized questionnaires

Guided, qualitative interviews with family members of patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
No questionnaires

Guided, qualitative interviews with healthcare providers treating patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (neurosurgery, anesthesiology, radiology, or rehabilitation clinics) 
No questionnaires

Focus groups
Patients and family members each form a focus group; the discussions in these groups, as well as the qualitative interviews, will be analyzed

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who have experienced an aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage 
OR
Caregivers of patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: Regularly provide supportive care—whether nursing, emotional, and/or organizational

    2. Age: ≥ 18 years
    3. Severity: WFNS grade ≤ III
    4. Language: Sufficient proficiency in German
    5. Sufficient cognitive function
    6. Capacity to give informed consent 

Treating physician: Experience in treating aSAH patients (neurosurgery, neuroradiology, or anesthesiology)
Exclusion criteria:
Additional untreated aneurysms
